thesis: USA Rare Earth is a strategic-theme vehicle racing to build a domestic mine-to-magnet supply chain: Stillwater magnet plant Phase 1a commissioned in March 2026 (targeting 600 tonnes/year by year-end), 100% ownership of the Round Top heavy-rare-earth deposit, a Carester processing-IP investment, $1.75B cash after a $1.5B PIPE, and a pending $2.8B Serra Verde acquisition. Against that: Q1 2026 revenue was just $5.7M at a 1.9% gross margin with a $67M net loss, while the market cap (~$4.2B) is ~180x annualized revenue. The -15.4% week (after a +9% print earlier) shows the tape trading policy headlines, not fundamentals.
catalysts: Stillwater ramp to 600 tonnes/year magnet run-rate by end of 2026
Serra Verde acquisition close (~$2.8B) - transforms the resource base
Carester heavy-rare-earth processing facility ramp late 2026 into 2027
US government/DoD rare-earth policy support (price floors, offtakes, stockpiling)
Round Top project milestones at 100% economic ownership
risk_factors: Economics unproven: $5.7M quarterly revenue at 1.9% gross margin - the business model has not yet demonstrated it can make money at any scale
The $2.8B Serra Verde deal is 2/3 the size of the company's own market cap - integration and funding risk dominate
Rare-earth pricing volatility and China's ability to crash prices on strategic competitors
Processing at scale is technologically hard (the reason the West exited the industry); execution risk is High
Cash burn: $18.6M operating + $38.6M capex in Q1 alone, accelerating with construction; the $1.75B buffer shrinks fast alongside a $2.8B acquisition
